# implement.py finish must not report a push failure when the commit landed on origin/dev

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` treats the exit status of `git push` as the sole verdict on
whether the commit reached `origin/dev`. When the push process is interrupted
(timeout, process-group kill, or a late non-zero exit) *after* the remote has
already accepted and updated the ref, `finish` wrongly reports
`git push to dev failed`, resets the work item from `in_progress` to `open`, and
leaves the operator/agent to reconcile a work item whose work is already on
`dev`. That false failure invites duplicate work and blocks the item from
reaching `in_review` even though nothing is left to do.

The fix is to make the push verdict **remote-observed**: before reporting a
failure, `finish` must check whether its commit is actually reachable from
`origin/dev`, and when it is, follow the normal success path (comment, worktree
cleanup/removal, parent-branch sync, `completed`/`in_review`).

## Users

- **Implementation agent** (`/skill:implement`, `implement.py finish`) — as the
  agent finishing a work item, I want a push that actually landed to be
  reported as success, so I do not retry completed work or hand the operator a
  false failure.
- **Epic driver / parent phase** (`implement.py drive`) — as the driver, I want
  a child whose commit is on `dev` to reach a terminal status, so the parent
  does not stall waiting for a child that is in fact finished.
- **Producer / operator** — as the producer, I want the work item state to
  reflect reality (work on `dev` ⇒ `completed`/`in_review`) and the finish
  report to distinguish "push failed", "push landed but the command was
  interrupted", and "push outcome unknown", so manual recovery is only needed
  when it truly is.
- **Audit / release gate** — as post-push verification, I want `in_review` to
  imply that the recorded commit is on `origin/dev`.

Example user stories:

> As an implementation agent, when the push command is killed at the timeout but
> `origin/dev` already points at my commit, I want `finish` to record the commit
> comment and leave the item `in_review` instead of resetting it to `open`.

> As an operator, when `finish` reports a push failure, I want the report to say
> whether the commit was verified absent from `origin/dev` or whether
> verification itself could not run, so I know exactly what recovery is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Remote-observed verdict.** Before `finish` reports a push failure
   (`PushTimeoutError`, process-group kill, or a non-zero `git push` exit that
   is not a non-fast-forward), it verifies whether the commit being pushed is
   reachable from the remote `dev` tip (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev`
   plus a fetch of that ref and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash>
   <remote-tip>`). The verification is time-bounded, uses only ref/object
   plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite), and
   applies to the non-fast-forward retry push as well as the first push.
   *Verification:* unit tests drive each interrupted-push variant and assert
   the verification probe runs before any failure is reported.
2. **Verified-landed = success, not failure.** When verification confirms the
   commit is on `origin/dev`, `finish` completes normally: it records the
   completion comment naming the commit, performs the existing success-path
   cleanup (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), leaves the
   work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal read-back still passes), and
   marks the report explicitly (e.g. `steps.push.verified_after_failure: true`
   plus the original error text) with an explanatory work-item comment.
   *Verification:* an end-to-end test against a hermetic bare remote + clone
   where the remote already contains the commit and the push hangs past a short
   timeout asserts `report["success"] is True`, the push step is marked
   verified, the commit comment is posted, and the item is `in_review`.
3. **Genuine failure and unknown outcome are preserved and distinguished.**
   When verification finds the commit absent from `origin/dev`, or when
   verification itself fails (e.g. `ls-remote` network error), `finish` still
   fails conservatively: status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree
   recovery comment is posted, and the worktree is **retained** (existing
   WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1 behaviour). The message/report distinguishes
   `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from
   `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, and never
   claims success without positive verification.
   *Verification:* negative tests (remote without the commit; verification
   probe failing) assert the item is reset to `open`, the worktree survives,
   and the distinct wording/report field appears.
4. **Regression coverage.** New tests are hermetic (self-contained bare remote +
   clone under `tmp_path`; no live checkout or live `refs/heads/dev` mutation)
   and cover: interrupted push that landed, interrupted push that did not land,
   verification probe failure, and a sibling push advancing `origin/dev` after
   ours (ancestry, not equality, must be accepted).
   *Verification:* the named tests exist, fail without the fix (or exercise the
   new helper directly), and pass with it.
5. **Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (push timeout / recovery
   section) and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` describe the
   remote-observed verdict, the three outcomes, and their recovery paths.
   *Verification:* doc review — both files describe the new behaviour and no
   longer state that a timeout always resets the item to `open`.
6. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (enforced at the
   dev-push gate). All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
   including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.

## Constraints

- **Positive verification only.** Never report success for a commit that was
  not observed on `origin/dev`; this must not weaken the terminal-status
  read-back guarantee (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58).
- **No pre-push hook on verification.** The pre-push hook runs the full suite
  (~minutes); verification must use `ls-remote`/`fetch` only and be bounded
  (recommended: ~60 s, short enough not to compound a stalled finish, long
  enough for a healthy remote). A verification fetch only updates
  remote-tracking refs, which the live-repo guard already excludes.
- **Ancestry, not equality.** Sibling sessions may push after ours; the commit
  is considered landed when it is an *ancestor* of the current `origin/dev`
  tip. Resolve the short hash recorded by `git_get_commit_hash()` to a full
  hash before the ancestry check.
- **No force-push, no history rewrite, no `reset --hard`** of the shared main
  checkout; recovery stays additive.
- **Preserve existing behaviour:** non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry
  (WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M), worktree retention on genuine failure
  (WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1), pre-push main-checkout mutation guard, and
  `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics must all keep working.
- **Coordinate, do not duplicate:** the post-*success* ancestry assertion is
  owned by SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U (parent SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY). Extract a single
  shared `_verify_commit_on_remote()` helper usable by both directions rather
  than shipping two divergent probes.
- **Test hermeticity:** tests must never mutate the live checkout's refs and
  must not depend on network access.
- **Report fields are additive.** `steps.push` keeps its existing
  `success`/`hash` keys (a cleanup test indexes the literal
  `report["steps"]["push"]` line); the verified-landed marker is a new
  optional key, never a renamed or repurposed one.
- **No workflow-language change:** the item must not alter the documented
  stage/status transitions, only which outcome (success vs failure) `finish`
  selects when the remote says the commit landed.
- **Source of truth:** the fix lands in this repository's
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the installed runtime copy at
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` only picks it up after
  `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Existing state

- `git_push_to_dev()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` L5629) spawns
  `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` in its own process group, with the
  timeout from `_resolve_test_timeout()` (`.pi/test-config.json`
  `timeoutPerCommand`; currently 2700 s, default 600 s). On `TimeoutExpired` it
  process-group-kills the push and raises `PushTimeoutError` (L4667); on a
  non-zero exit it raises `PushNonFastForwardError` when the stderr matches
  non-fast-forward wording, otherwise logs `git push to dev failed` and returns
  `False`. There is no post-failure remote check.
- `phase_finish()` (L11198) Step 6 (L12011) maps a `False` return to
  `RuntimeError("git push to dev failed.")`, posts a manual-push comment on
  `PushTimeoutError`, and the outer `RuntimeError` handler resets status to
  `open`. Steps 6b–8 (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync)
  and the `StatusLifecycle(target_stage="in_review")` exit only run after a
  successful push; `_assert_terminal_status()` (L985) then re-reads the store.
- `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050) rebases in the worktree, retries
  `git_push_to_dev()`, and reports the rewritten hash. A retry that lands but
  is reported as failed has the same false-failure problem.
- `_sync_parent_branch()` (L7149) already uses
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`, showing the
  ancestry idiom in use.
- `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084) already performs the post-*success*
  ancestry assertion in **Step 6a** (L12271), which SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U shipped
  (now completed). It is the only remote check today and it runs *after* a push
  claimed success, so it cannot distinguish "landed but interrupted" from
  "never landed". The new probe must be **extracted** from this helper (one
  shared `_verify_commit_on_remote()`), not added beside it.
- Existing tests: `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` (timeout config,
  process-group kill, recoverable state),
  `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` (ordering: push precedes
  worktree removal, recovery end-to-end),
  `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` (terminal read-back).
  None simulate "remote already updated, push command interrupted".
- Observed incident (SA-0MUOO5UEB008RXBP): `finish` reported
  `git push to dev failed`, reset the item to `open` and removed the worktree,
  while `origin/dev == dev == 4b25aac4` already contained the new file.
- A companion ToneForge observation (TF-0MUYFYF7Q007BLCX) noted worktree removal
  on a failed push; that ordering has since been fixed (push before removal),
  so no new worktree-lifecycle change is required here beyond retaining it.

## Desired change

1. Add `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout=...) -> bool | None`
   in `implement.py`: resolve the full hash, read `origin`'s
   `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetch that ref when the tip differs
   (bounded), and return `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says the
   commit is reachable, `False` when positively absent, `None` when the probe
   itself failed (network/auth/timeout).
2. Route every non-success push outcome through that probe. Recommended shape:
   have `git_push_to_dev()` raise a distinct "interrupted but verified landed"
   signal (or return an outcome object) rather than `False`/`PushTimeoutError`,
   so `phase_finish` can mark `steps.push.verified_after_failure`, comment, and
   continue on the success path; `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` handles the
   same signal on its retry.
3. Keep the conservative failure paths unchanged (`open`, manual-push comment,
   worktree retained) with the unknown-outcome wording when the probe returns
   `None`.
4. Extract the probe so the post-success ancestry assertion
   (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U) can reuse it, and note the reuse in both items.
5. Document the three outcomes in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

**Success metric:** zero false push-failure reports in which the recorded
commit is reachable from `origin/dev`; every genuine failure still names the
commit/branch and leaves recovery state intact.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (L5629),
  `PushTimeoutError` (L4667), `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050),
  `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011), `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084);
  new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` helper shared by both.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — extend interrupted-push coverage;
  or add `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` for the new
  remote-verdict tests (hermetic bare remote + clone).
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push path must
  also treat a verified-landed interruption as success.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Push timeout" section (L1436).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish / push-to-dev guidance (≈ L329–L371;
  the old L235–L253 push-recovery prose now lives in the reference doc).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUH9R74O002MQDU** (completed) — made the push timeout configurable,
  killed hook children, and left recoverable state. This item fixes the false
  verdict that item's design still allows; it must not regress AC1–AC3 there.
- **SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY** (completed) — concurrent sessions orphaning commits
  via the shared local-dev fast-forward; shipped the per-repository `finish`
  lock and verified local-dev sync. The lock holds across this item's extra
  probe, which only reads refs.
- **SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U** (completed) — post-*success* ancestry assertion,
  shipped as `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` + Step 6a. Complementary
  direction (false success); the probe is extracted from it so the two
  directions share one implementation.
- **SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5** (open, `plan_complete`) — its AC3 converges a
  `finish` whose commit is *already* an ancestor of `origin/dev` before any
  push is attempted (plus transport classification). This item covers the
  complementary path: a push command that ran and was reported as failed.
  Both need the same remote read, so `_verify_commit_on_remote()` is the
  shared probe; neither item should ship a second one.
- **SA-0MW98UNVB0085LFA** (open, `plan_complete`) — attributes a *prior-run*
  commit on an interrupted-push re-run (no new commit created). Distinct
  concern: attribution, not the push verdict this item fixes.
- **SA-0MVLJXS7R000XIFL** (completed) — bounds repeated failing `finish`
  attempts; a false failure fed that loop, so this fix reduces the loop's
  blast radius.
- **SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG** (completed) — live-repo guard attribution of
  concurrent-session churn; the verification fetch touches only
  remote-tracking refs, which the guard excludes.
- **SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM** (completed) — driven-child worktree escape
  incident; the ToneForge duplicate report (TF-0MUYFYF7Q007BLCX) was split
  from it and supplied the worktree-retention observation.
- **WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1** and **WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M** — referenced in the code
  and docs for push-before-removal ordering and non-fast-forward recovery
  (records live in another project's worklog, not resolvable here).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** a push can land yet be reported as failed (observed:
  SA-0MUOO5UEB008RXBP). The verification probe is the correct discriminator;
  it also degrades safely when no such race occurs.
- **Assumption:** `origin` is the canonical remote for `dev`, as assumed
  throughout `implement.py`; no multi-remote support is added.
- **Assumption:** verification is read-only w.r.t. shared refs — a fetch updates
  `refs/remotes/origin/*` only — so it does not trip the main-checkout mutation
  guard.
- **Risk:** the probe's own network call can stall or fail; it is bounded and
  its failure maps to the conservative "unknown" outcome.
- **Risk:** sibling pushes can advance `origin/dev` between probe steps; using
  the freshly read tip and ancestry (not equality) avoids false negatives.
- **Risk:** short-hash ambiguity in the report/comment; resolve to a full hash
  for the check while keeping the short hash in human-facing text.
- **Risk (scope creep):** redesigning the push/lock architecture belongs to
  SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY; this item only adds the verdict check. Any further
  hardening discovered during implementation is filed as a linked item rather
  than folded in.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed report, the companion comment,
and repository research supplied enough detail to draft testable acceptance
criteria. The assumptions are recorded above and are open to producer
correction without changing the intent.

- Q: *What is the dominant failure mode being fixed?* — Answer (seed report,
  SA-0MUOO5UEB008RXBP): a push that landed on `origin/dev` while `finish`
  reported `git push to dev failed` and reset the item to `open`. Source:
  work-item description.
- Q: *Does the companion observation (worktree removed on a failed push) still
  need work?* — Answer (repo research): no — Step 6 now runs the push before
  Step 7's worktree removal, so a failed push retains the worktree
  (`implement.py` Step 6–7, L12011–L12360, commit `6229a0605`,
  WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1). Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py::TestFinishOrdering`.
- Q: *Is there an existing post-push remote check to reuse?* — Answer (repo
  research): partially. `_sync_parent_branch()` (L7149) uses
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor` for the local parent branch, and the
  post-success ancestry assertion SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U **has since landed**
  (completed) as `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084) + Step 6a
  (L12271). Revision: the probe is therefore **extracted** from that helper
  and reused, rather than written fresh beside it.
  Source: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` L7149, L8084, L12271; work
  item SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U (completed).
- Q: *Is this a duplicate of an existing item?* — Answer (duplicate check):
  no. SA-0MUH9R74O002MQDU (completed) fixed timeout configuration, process-group
  kill and recoverable state but still treats an interrupted push as a failure;
  SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U covers the opposite (false-success) direction and is
  completed. Source: `wl show` on both items.

## Plan: changelog

Plan session 2026-11-11 (`/skill:plan SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX`). Pre-check:
effort Small / risk Medium → full planning required; approval gate not
requested (approval needs Extra Large **and** High/Severe).

- Decomposed into three dependency-ordered slices, test-first:
  - **SA-0MWCE5XKV0027468** — Hermetic interrupted-push verdict tests (`task`).
  - **SA-0MWCE5ZBR009WC53** — Remote-observed push verdict in finish (`bug`);
    depends on SA-0MWCE5XKV0027468.
  - **SA-0MWCE61RC000L15T** — Document remote-observed push verdict (`docs`);
    depends on SA-0MWCE5ZBR009WC53.
- AC coverage review: 6/6 parent ACs covered (100%); recommendation `proceed`.
- No clarifying questions were needed; the description already carried the
  desired change and constraints, so no producer input was requested.
- Duplicate check: no full duplicate. Partial overlaps recorded in **Related
  work** and kept out of scope — SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5 AC3 (already-landed
  convergence before a push is attempted) and SA-0MW98UNVB0085LFA (prior-run
  commit attribution). Both share `_verify_commit_on_remote()`.
- Conservative corrections applied during the automated review stages: stale
  line references in **Existing state** / **Key Files** (verified against
  HEAD), the corrected status of related items (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U,
  SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY, SA-0MVLJXS7R000XIFL and SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG are
  completed), the new `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` existing-state bullet,
  and current documentation anchors. No requirement or AC text was changed
  (AC1–AC6 are unchanged).

### Plan-session appendix (questions & answers)

No operator interview was required: the seed description supplied testable acceptance
criteria, a desired change and key files, and repository research answered the remaining
planning questions. Recorded for auditability:

- Q: *Do the child slices already exist?* — Answer (repo research + `wl list --parent`):
  no children existed; three were created (`SA-0MWCE5XKV0027468`,
  `SA-0MWCE5ZBR009WC53`, `SA-0MWCE61RC000L15T`).
- Q: *Which test harness should the new tests use?* — Answer (repo research):
  `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (`init_bare_remote`, `init_repo`, `add_worktree`,
  `commit_all`), as used by `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py`;
  end-to-end `phase_finish` slices follow the `FakeGitBoundary` style in
  `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`.
- Q: *Is the probe a duplicate of anything already shipped?* — Answer (`wl show` +
  code): partly — `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084) is the post-*success*
  assertion and must be re-pointed at the new shared probe; SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5 AC3
  covers the already-landed-before-push case, so only one probe is added here.
- **OPEN QUESTION: none.** Nothing blocks implementation.

# Hermetic interrupted-push verdict tests

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Test-first tracer bullet: write the regression tests **before** the fix. Expectations that
target the new behaviour carry `xfail(strict=True)` until the implementation child removes
the marker; expectations that already hold (the conservative failure paths, the
ancestry-not-equality rule) pass before and after, so a failing test can only be failing on
the behaviour under test.

## Goal

As an implementation agent, I want hermetic, deterministic tests that pin the remote-observed
push verdict, so a later change to `finish`'s push-outcome handling can never silently regress
into reporting a landed push as a failure — nor into claiming success for a commit that never
reached `origin/dev`.

## Context

`finish` treats the exit status of `git push` as the sole verdict on whether the commit reached
`origin/dev`, so a push interrupted after the remote accepted the ref (timeout, process-group
kill, late non-zero exit) is reported as a failure and the item is reset to `open`. The only
remote check today is the post-*success* ancestry assertion
(`_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()`, `implement.py` L8084), which runs after a push already
claimed success — nothing distinguishes "landed but interrupted" from "never landed". No
existing test simulates the race: `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py`,
`tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` and
`skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` all assume the push verdict is truthful.

## Scope

Tests only — no production-code change in this slice. Deliver the failing baselines that the
implementation child turns green, plus the companion tests that prove the preconditions (a
real hermetic push, a reachable bare remote, a real terminal read-back) rather than assuming
them.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — new hermetic suite: probe variants, the three outcomes, sibling-push ancestry.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — existing interrupted-push coverage; extend where a case belongs there.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push baseline (a retry that lands but is reported as failed).
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — reusable `init_bare_remote` / `init_repo` / `add_worktree` / `commit_all` factories; reuse rather than hand-rolling fixtures.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the `FakeGitBoundary` stubbed-boundary harness style for end-to-end `phase_finish` tests.

## Constraints

- **Hermetic:** self-contained bare remote plus clone/worktree under `tmp_path`; never mutate the live checkout's refs, never touch the shared `refs/heads/dev`, no network access.
- **Unambiguous baselines:** pair each new-behaviour `xfail(strict=True)` with a companion that passes before and after, so the preconditions are proven separately instead of being smuggled into the baseline.
- **No hiding failures:** `xfail(strict=True)` only where the expectation targets the not-yet-implemented behaviour.
- **Test execution policy:** no agent-initiated `pytest`/`run_tests.py` invocation outside `/skill:test` (`implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate and the dev-push gate are infrastructure and out of scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Interrupted push variants are covered by unit tests.** Unit tests drive each interrupted-push variant — `PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, and a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward — and assert the remote verification probe runs before any push failure is reported: it verifies whether the commit being pushed is reachable from the remote `dev` tip (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev` plus a fetch of that ref and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>`), is time-bounded, uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite), and applies to the non-fast-forward retry push as well as the first push.
- **Verified-landed success end-to-end.** An end-to-end hermetic test against a bare remote plus a clone under `tmp_path` — where the remote already contains the commit and the push hangs past a short timeout — asserts `report["success"] is True`, the push step is marked `verified_after_failure`, the completion comment naming the commit is posted, the existing success-path cleanup runs (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), and the work item is `completed`/`in_review` with the terminal read-back still passing.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome are distinguished.** Negative tests — a remote without the commit, and a verification probe that itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error) — assert `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Hermetic regression coverage, ancestry not equality.** The new tests are hermetic (self-contained bare remote plus clone under `tmp_path`; no live checkout or live `refs/heads/dev` mutation, no network access) and cover an interrupted push that landed, an interrupted push that did not land, a verification probe failure, and a sibling push advancing `origin/dev` after ours (ancestry, not equality, must be accepted); they fail without the fix (or exercise the new helper directly) and pass with it, reusing the `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` factories.

# Remote-observed push verdict in finish

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Builds on the test-first slice (the hermetic baselines land first; this slice makes them pass
and removes their `xfail(strict=True)` markers).

## Goal

As an implementation agent, when the push command is killed at the timeout but `origin/dev`
already points at my commit, I want `finish` to record the completion comment and leave the
item `completed`/`in_review` instead of resetting it to `open`; and as the producer, when
`finish` does report a push failure I want the report to say whether the commit was verified
**absent** from `origin/dev` or whether verification itself could not run, so I know exactly
what recovery is needed.

## Context

`git_push_to_dev()` (`implement.py` L5629) spawns `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` in
its own process group. On `TimeoutExpired` it process-group-kills the push and raises
`PushTimeoutError` (L4667); on a non-zero exit it raises `PushNonFastForwardError` for
non-fast-forward wording, otherwise logs `git push to dev failed` and returns `False`. There is
no post-failure remote check. `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011) maps a `False` return to
`RuntimeError("git push to dev failed.")`, posts a manual-push comment on `PushTimeoutError`,
and the outer `RuntimeError` handler resets the status to `open`; steps 6a–8 (post-push
ancestry assertion, cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync) and the
`StatusLifecycle(target_stage="in_review")` exit run only after a successful push.
`_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050) retries the push inside the worktree and has the
same false-failure exposure.

## Desired change

1. Add `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout=...) -> bool | None`: resolve the
   full hash, read `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetch that ref when the
   tip differs (bounded), and return `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says the commit
   is reachable, `False` when positively absent, `None` when the probe itself failed
   (network/auth/timeout).
2. Route every non-success push outcome through that probe. Recommended shape: have
   `git_push_to_dev()` raise a distinct "interrupted but verified landed" signal (or return an
   outcome object) rather than `False`/`PushTimeoutError`, so `phase_finish` can mark
   `steps.push.verified_after_failure`, comment, and continue on the success path;
   `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` handles the same signal on its retry.
3. Keep the conservative failure paths unchanged (`open`, manual-push comment, worktree
   retained) with the unknown-outcome wording when the probe returns `None`.
4. Extract the probe so the existing post-*success* ancestry assertion
   `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084, SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U, now completed) reuses it
   rather than shipping a second divergent probe; note the reuse on both items.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (L5629), `PushTimeoutError` (L4667), `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050), `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011), `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084); new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` helper.
- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — the baselines from the test-first slice.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — interrupted-push coverage.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push path.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the annotation noting the fake must keep resolving a published commit.

## Constraints

- **Positive verification only.** Never report success for a commit that was not observed on `origin/dev`; do not weaken the terminal-status read-back guarantee (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58).
- **No pre-push hook on verification.** The hook runs the full suite (~minutes); verification uses `ls-remote`/`fetch`/`merge-base` only and is bounded (recommended ~60 s). A verification fetch updates only remote-tracking refs, which the live-repo guard already excludes.
- **Ancestry, not equality.** Sibling sessions may push after ours; the commit is landed when it is an *ancestor* of the current `origin/dev` tip. Resolve the short hash from `git_get_commit_hash()` to a full hash before the ancestry check.
- **No force-push, no history rewrite, no `reset --hard`** of the shared main checkout; recovery stays additive.
- **Preserve existing behaviour:** non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry (WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M), worktree retention on genuine failure (WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1), pre-push main-checkout mutation guard, and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics.
- **Report fields are additive.** `steps.push` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (a cleanup test indexes the literal push step); the verified-landed marker is a new optional key, never a renamed or repurposed one.
- **No workflow-language change:** only which outcome (success vs failure) `finish` selects when the remote says the commit landed.
- **Source of truth:** the fix lands in this repository's `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the installed copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` picks it up only after `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared remote-verification probe.** A new `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout) -> bool | None` helper in `implement.py` resolves the full hash (resolving the short hash returned by `git_get_commit_hash()`), reads `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetches that ref when the tip differs (bounded, ~60 s), and returns `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>` reports the commit reachable, `False` when positively absent, and `None` when the probe itself failed (network/auth/timeout).
- **Remote-observed verdict before any failure report.** Before `finish` reports a push failure (`PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, or a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward), every non-success outcome is routed through the probe — including the non-fast-forward retry push in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` — and the verification is time-bounded and uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite).
- **Verified landed is success, not failure.** When verification confirms the commit is on `origin/dev`, `finish` completes normally: it records the completion comment naming the commit, performs the existing success-path cleanup (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), leaves the work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal read-back still passes), and marks the report explicitly (`steps.push.verified_after_failure: true` plus the original error text) with an explanatory work-item comment.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome stay conservative.** When verification finds the commit absent from `origin/dev`, or verification itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error), `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message/report distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Ancestry, additive fields, preserved behaviour, no duplicate probe.** The commit is considered landed when it is an ancestor of the current `origin/dev` tip, never equality; the probe is extracted so the existing post-success ancestry assertion `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U) reuses it instead of shipping a divergent second probe; non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry, worktree retention on genuine failure, the pre-push main-checkout mutation guard and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics keep working; and `report["steps"]["push"]` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (new keys are additive only).

# Document remote-observed push verdict

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Documentation slice for the remote-observed push verdict. It follows the implementation slice
so it describes the shipped behaviour (the new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` probe, the report
fields, and the three outcomes) rather than a planned one.

## Goal

As an operator or implementation agent reading the finish documentation, I want the three push
outcomes and their recovery paths stated explicitly, so I never retry completed work and never
manually push a commit that is already on `origin/dev`.

## Context

The current "Push timeout" section of `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (L1436) says a
timeout "resets status to `open`" and posts a manual-push comment — that is exactly the false
failure this parent fixes. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` describes `finish`'s behaviour around
L329–L371 but says nothing about a push verdict being verified against the remote.

## Scope

Documentation only: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, and
any code comment the implementation slice leaves inconsistent. No behaviour change.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Push timeout" section (L1436) and the push-failure table entries.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish / push-to-dev guidance (L329–L371).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` — doc-hygiene guard to re-run.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — code comments in the push-outcome handlers.

## Constraints

- Describe only behaviour that the implementation slice actually ships; no speculative or aspirational wording.
- Keep the existing document structure and cross-reference style; do not restructure unrelated sections.
- UK English, and no claim that a timeout always resets the item to `open`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Both documentation files describe the remote-observed verdict.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (push timeout / recovery section) and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` describe the remote-observed verdict, the three outcomes, and their recovery paths, so a doc review confirms both files describe the new behaviour and no longer state that a timeout always resets the item to `open`. The reference doc's "Push timeout" section (≈ L1436) additionally records the bounded `ls-remote`/`fetch`/`git merge-base --is-ancestor` probe that never runs the pre-push hook or the test suite.
- **`skill/implement/SKILL.md` states the three outcomes and their recovery.** The finish/push-to-dev guidance (≈ L329–L371) states that a `finish` report names which of the three outcomes occurred, that a push the remote verification confirms as landed completes normally (`completed`/`in_review`) rather than being reported as a failure, and that a genuine failure retains the worktree and requires a manual push.
- **Full project test suite passes and all related documentation is updated.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate), and all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries; doc-hygiene tests under `skill/implement/tests/` (e.g. `test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py`) still pass.
